# Normativity Analysis Quality Checklist

> After each normativity analysis, check each item. A fully checked list indicates a high-quality analysis.

---

## Ought-Type Classification

- [ ] **Complete extraction**: Have all normative claims (explicit and implicit) been extracted from the reconstructed argument?
- [ ] **Domain accuracy**: Is each claim classified to the correct domain (moral, prudential, epistemic, instrumental, aesthetic, legal, social)?
- [ ] **Categorical/hypothetical precision**: Has the Kantian test been applied to each claim, with the basis for the classification stated?
- [ ] **Descriptive "ought" exclusion**: Have purely descriptive/predictive/epistemic-modal uses of "ought" been excluded and listed separately?
- [ ] **Reductionist strategy noted**: If apparently categorical claims are reduced to hypothetical form, has this been flagged?

## Source Identification

- [ ] **Evidence-supported**: Is each source classification (constitutivist, Humean, rationalist, etc.) supported by specific textual or structural evidence?
- [ ] **Domain-specific sourcing**: If the argument mixes source theories across domains, has each domain-source pair been separately documented?
- [ ] **Nearest-neighbor distinguished**: Has the classification been refined to the specific version, not merely the broad category?
- [ ] **Alternative diagnoses noted**: Where the evidence underdetermines classification, has the range of compatible positions been stated?

## Categorical/Hypothetical Distinction

- [ ] **Test properly applied**: Has the conditional reformulation test been explicitly applied for each normative claim?
- [ ] **Borderline cases discussed**: Have formally-hypothetical-but-substantively-categorical claims been identified and explained?
- [ ] **Inescapability analyzed**: For claims resting on inescapable conditions, has the claim of inescapability been evaluated?

## Internal/External Reasons Assessment

- [ ] **Explicit position check**: Has the argument been checked for an explicit statement on reasons internalism/externalism?
- [ ] **Implicit inference justified**: If inferred from structural features, are the diagnostic questions explicitly applied?
- [ ] **Strength level specified**: Has the specific form been identified (strong/weak motivational, rational, Humean, strong/moderate external)?
- [ ] **Domain-dependence noted**: If internalism/externalism varies by domain, has this been documented?
- [ ] **Tension flagged**: If internalism/externalism diagnosis conflicts with source theory diagnosis, has this been flagged?

## Normative Architecture Analysis

- [ ] **Architecture type justified**: Is the classification (foundational, coherentist, hierarchical, network) supported by the structural map?
- [ ] **Full relation mapping**: Are all support, dependency, and tension relations among normative claims documented?
- [ ] **Foundational claims identified**: If foundational architecture, are the axioms clearly indicated?
- [ ] **Orphans flagged**: Have normative claims with no upstream or downstream relations been noted?
- [ ] **Conflict resolution addressed**: If conflicts exist, has the absence or presence of a resolution mechanism been documented?

## Bindingness & Regress

- [ ] **Full chain traced**: Has the "because" chain been traced for the central normative claim(s)?
- [ ] **Regress-stopper identified**: Has the terminus of the normative chain been located?
- [ ] **Regress-stopper adequacy evaluated**: Has the terminus been assessed for whether asking "but why should I care?" would be coherent?
- [ ] **Gaps flagged**: If the argument does not address the regress, has this been noted?

## Report Quality

- [ ] **Executive summary concise**: Does the summary in 2-4 sentences capture the primary diagnosis and key tensions?
- [ ] **Domain conflation flagged**: If the argument conflates normative domains, is this explicitly identified?
- [ ] **Metaethical implications stated**: Does the report conclude with explicit implications for downstream analysis?
- [ ] **Confidence levels annotated**: Are all diagnostic judgments accompanied by confidence levels (high/medium/low)?
- [ ] **Boundary conditions respected**: Has the report checked whether the argument falls under any boundary condition (no normative language, purely first-order, error-theoretic)?
